column4: Review failed open in the landing path: train.sh check set review=0 when no review command existed (no error), its review leg rejected only a published findings note (absent, malformed or blocked passed after a zero exit), and land read no review record at all, so a check run with --no-review landed like any other (facts-decision landed at ab537833d after train.sh check --no-review). Structural cause: review was enforced only as one leg's exit status inside check, a missing reviewer was mapped to a disabled leg, and land trusted CI alone: no reader of review provenance existed at land time. Fixed on wip/fix-landing-machinery (a173432e): check fails with no review command; review_provenance (verify.sh on origin's notes: a clean head note, or with no head note a clean note on every member at its exact SHA) gates both the review leg and land

column4: scripts/land/acceptance.sh's check leg ran train.sh check --no-review --no-remote, so an accepted rehearsal (the record the move gate trusts) could rest on a check that skipped review, and agents cannot run it (the permission system treats --no-review as a CI bypass); both its build leg and its broken-build control defaulted to make build, which the restarted root (no Makefile; nix develop --command lake build) does not have; its header described only --no-review and make build. Fixed on wip/fix-landing-machinery (9b48910f): check --no-remote with the review leg passing on verified notes; one BUILD_CMD default for both build legs; header corrected; a landing_script.sh structural control

column4: Sandboxes inherit the caller's git environment. scripts/checks/review_tool.sh isolated git config only, not the repository-locating variables; a pre-push hook of a LINKED worktree exports GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>, so every git -C <sandbox> in the check acted on the caller. On 2026-11-06 `train.sh ci laudit` run from the linked worktree ~agent/audit-records made the hook's review_tool.sh create its test branches (nonff, capped, parse-*) and set core.bare=true in ~agent/audit-clone (kept unchanged as evidence), and push 28 commits to origin refs/notes/concrete-review (tip b4b364f4, pre-leak 5b6add0d) and 12 to refs/notes/concrete-review-findings (tip 21c56796, pre-leak fd3c6451), authored Review Gate, 17:16:49-17:17:43Z, annotating 21 sandbox commits that exist on no remote (first counted as 22, which wrongly included c54679c3, a real commit whose note at 17:21Z is legitimate); no earlier note was deleted or changed and every reader looks notes up by exact SHA, so none can count as provenance for a real commit. lambdaclass has no notes refs. Codex confirmed with a bounded reproducer on concrete-ci-2 at main f9a8c333 (caller refs and refs/notes/* changed: LEAK) and an independent GIT_DIR experiment. landing_script.sh and landing_bot.sh unset only five of git's local variables; legacy_frozen.sh, acceptance.sh, run-at-ref.sh and bot.sh unset none. Second incident, same cause: the first reproducer installed a pre-push hook that ran review_tool.sh; the leaked GIT_DIR made each nested push re-enter that hook, the recursion exhausted fede-256gb (load ~1900) and the OOM killer took down the orchestrator's session. Structural owner: the sandbox helper scripts/checks/lib/git_sandbox.sh (unsets every `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` variable), sourced by every repository-making script; reproducers and tests run with no installed hook, under timeout 120 and a 512-task / 8G systemd scope bound, or a finite cgroup memory.max plus a process limit, and never an unbounded run. Closed 2026-11-07: the fix landed at dbe838488891, where every closure part is checked in Root checks (scripts/checks/run.sh, all 11 pass: sandbox_isolation PASS=13 FAIL=0 with its structural leg over 9 scripts, the two live linked-worktree probes and the leaking control; landing_script PASS=208 FAIL=0 with the linked-worktree, hook-off, foreign-hook and identify refusal legs; also run on concrete-ci-2 at 8e62e377) (train siso from a full clone; reviewed by Codex, rounds clean at 8e62e377, and Kimi; CI run 42424663064; main CI 42425007584 on origin and 42425010605 on lambdaclass, both success). The stray notes were removed from origin by one forward fast-forward commit per ref on its then-current tip, no force: refs/notes/concrete-review d4bdcae22d50 -> dcffeea8e6cd (21 entries removed, 224 untouched at the push; Codex confirmed the list against the earlier tip 8cbb7db253f7, where 223 were untouched, and the one commit between that tip and d4bdcae22d50 only added a legitimate note for 9d6dc01a, so the removal list is identical) and refs/notes/concrete-review-findings 301e929e1bab -> 5d7c6dc3dad5 (11 removed, 105 untouched); the 40 leaked commits wrote 33 entries, one of which they removed themselves (0c04c01c); Codex confirmed the removal list and the tree diffs before the push; lambdaclass has no notes refs and none were created. ~agent/audit-clone is kept unchanged as evidence with LEAK-EVIDENCE-README.txt
column7: every repository-making script under scripts/ sources git_sandbox.sh (scripts/checks/sandbox_isolation.sh, structural leg); review_tool.sh and legacy_frozen.sh run from a linked worktree with GIT_DIR exported leave the caller's refs, refs/notes/*, core.bare and upstream unchanged while a leaking control is detected (same check, bounded); train.sh and the pre-push hook refuse a linked worktree and train.sh refuses a clone without the repository hook; and the stray notes are removed from origin by a forward fast-forward notes commit whose before and after tips are recorded here

column4: CI run 42424028055 (train legacydocs at 4d0355a56e, a docs-only change over 93850111) failed Kernel replay (leanchecker): the per-module leg replayed ConcreteSpec.Spec.Ownership, a module renamed to Slice1Ownership by 44ee1231, and stopped on unknown constant 'ConcreteSpec.lookupF'. The job's lake cache had been restored through a restore-key prefix from the cache of train commit 5b894432ad, whose sources predate the rename. Non-fresh `leanchecker ConcreteSpec` picks every .olean on the search path whose name has the prefix (the toolchain's LeanChecker.lean, lines 91-94), so orphaned build files are replayed. Reproducer: build 44ee1231^, build 93850111's sources over that build directory, run scripts/proofs/kernel_replay.sh: FAIL on the Checker/Syntax orphans; a clean build of the same sources passes. Codex confirmed it with that reproducer (2026-11-07). Structural cause: the replay took its module list from the build directory's contents instead of the sources.
column7: closed by wip/replay-source-modules: kernel_replay.sh replays a staged library holding exactly the modules the sources declare and checks that the replayed set equals that list; scripts/proofs/lib.sh prunes build files of modules with no source before building; negative controls plant an orphan that fails an unfiltered replay and is ignored by the staged one

column4: Codex confirmed: Memory.WellFormed checked only lookup, whereas fromExposed scans all entries; [(b, deadBlock), (b, exposedLiveBlock)] could hide a contradictory candidate from lookup. Structural cause: association-list representation lacked a canonical-entry invariant.

column4: agy (CTy consult, 2026-11-08) found that C2 models `tryConvert` in constant initializers as scalar-returning: `CExpr.tryConvert` (ConcreteSpec/Spec/Const.lean:81) is typed by `CExpr.ty?` as the unwrapped scalar (Const.lean:441-443) and its evaluation turns a failed conversion into a refusal of the constant, while OD106 (docs/decisions.md:1214, 1221) gives the surface `try_convert` the type `Result<T, OutOfRange>`. The spec therefore models a surface operation that does not exist, against TYPE-4@2 (every expression has exactly one type) and PHILOSOPHY Rule 2. Closed 2026-11-09: round 7 commit 07534c258908ecb0b5435eec9aaba0144eb56f44 (spec: restrict constant initializers to scalar surface operations) removes tryConvert from CExpr and its semantics under owner decision 2026-11-09 item 2, options (a)+(i); constants remain scalar and aggregate/enum constants are the sole reopening path.
column5: C2 CExpr.tryConvert (ConcreteSpec/Spec/Const.lean); owner question C2 constants
column7: The owner answers the C2 constants question. Under (a)+(i) (constants scalar; initializers use only operations whose surface type is scalar), tryConvert leaves CExpr until the reopening path (c). Under (ii), it is replaced by an owner-decided scalar-returning, refusing conversion.

column4: ConcreteSpec/Spec/Observe.lean:278-307 (byteColumn, sourceSpan, scanSourcePrefix, sourcePrefixSpan, Span.HasByteColumn) independently constructs coordinates beside ConcreteSpec/Spec/Ident.lean:695-702 (SourceText.lineAt, columnAt) and :812-814 (Span.LocationOk). Codex confirmation of the aa44140a3 audit: s1a-2 and confirmed coordinate part of s1b-1. Structural cause: character-prefix construction predates the shared byte model and has no correspondence law; sourceSpan is explicitly a prefix-relative candidate, not an admission guarantee. Design: docs/proposals/ISS-0045-SOURCE-COORDINATES.md.
column7: Give byte-derived coordinates one authoritative owner; constructors delegate to it or prove correspondence under explicit UTF-8-prefix, offset and line premises (including the candidate API restrictions). Every retained view has a premise-preserving mutant that breaks coordinate agreement while retaining its premises, covering newline, multibyte and tab cases; otherwise delete the redundant view.

column4: ConcreteSpec/Spec/Prim.lean:91-101 (Prim.lookupId, Term.eval) compares numeric ids; ConcreteSpec/Spec/Basics.lean:27-29 (AList.lookup) and ConcreteSpec/Spec/Exec.lean:364-366 (assignment) compare whole Var values, whose equality includes hints at ConcreteSpec/Spec/Ident.lean:41-44. Codex confirmation of the aa44140a3 audit: s1a-3, s1c-3, identity part of s2-1. Executed same-id/different-hint example: "ConcreteSpec.Core.Res.ok 7" versus "none". Structural cause: the operand adapter independently selects identity while environment operations retain presentation-bearing keys; no common identity contract. This establishes raw-model disagreement, not that elaboration produces mismatched hints.
column7: Owner first answers: does variable identity depend only on the numeric id, or on both id and hint (and what consistency premise is required)? Implement that answer with one authoritative identity/lookup policy across primitive operands and assignment; any retained view proves correspondence under the same explicit premises and has a premise-preserving identity mutant; the executed different-hint case and assignment conformance check enforce the approved answer.

column4: ConcreteSpec/Spec/Observe.lean:167-169 (SiteTable.Valid), :251-256 (ProjectSources.Realizes), keep overlapping source obligations separately; :576-589 (ExecAdapter.WellFormed) separately specifies event/request obligations, while ExecAdapter.loaded at :461 carries source admission. Codex confirmation of the aa44140a3 audit: confirmed invariant-ownership part of s1b-2. Structural cause: lookup-visible coordinate validity and whole-input admission independently maintain overlapping correspondence obligations; shadowed entries escape lookup validity but duplicate keys are rejected by the loader at :241-244. Existing admitted-adapter validity bridge at ConcreteSpec/Proofs/Observe2.lean:1075-1082 prevents claiming admitted malformed tables. Design: docs/proposals/ISS-0047-SITE-TABLE-OBLIGATIONS.md.
column7: Give shared site/source correspondence one authoritative predicate and reuse it in admission and adapter obligations, retaining exact-input preservation and uniqueness as distinct requirements. Each retained view proves correspondence with its precise lookup-visible or whole-table premises; premise-preserving shadowed-entry and coordinate mutants must fail the appropriate correspondence/admission checks, or redundant predicates are deleted.

column4: ConcreteSpec/Spec/Observe.lean:350-351 (Observe.launch) selects S.initState on refusal, while :639-647 (launchObservation) selects A.state c.store; ExecAdapter at :454-461 and WellFormed at :576-589 impose no initial-state equality. Demo.signature at :711-717 has initial state 0. Codex confirmation of the aa44140a3 audit: state part of s1b-4. Executed refusal-state projection: "some 0"; (Observe.Environment.adapter Observe.Demo.signature).state 1: "1". Structural cause: signature initialization and store-state projection are unconstrained independent launch-state representations.
column7: Owner first answers: must startup refusal expose the signature initial state or the supplied store projection, and which initial-store premises are required? Give refusal-state selection one authoritative definition implementing that answer; launch and launchObservation delegate or prove correspondence under explicit approved premises, with a premise-preserving state-selection mutant and a conformance check covering store 1 against signature initial state 0.

column4: ConcreteSpec/Spec/Prim.lean:407-432 (Ghost.SegmentReport, Ghost.drive) copies the fuel/oracle/contract/continuation dispatch of ConcreteSpec/Spec/Exec.lean:842-866 (Exec.Report, Exec.runFrom) while retaining configuration and fuel. Codex confirmation of the aa44140a3 audit: s1c-2, s2-2. Structural cause: Exec.Report omits residual configuration and fuel needed for composition, prompting another executable driver. ConcreteSpec/Proofs/Prim.lean:299-304 proves step-path soundness but not equality of report endings and histories for the same budget. Design: docs/proposals/ISS-0049-GHOST-DRIVER.md.
column7: Give fuel-indexed execution one authoritative driver exposing residual configuration and fuel, with ordinary and ghost reports derived from it; otherwise prove complete report-projection correspondence for all shared inputs. Any retained driver view has a premise-preserving dispatch mutant that breaks correspondence, covering finality, zero fuel, silent steps, absent/bad answers, continuations, event accumulation and unused fuel; delete the unchecked copy.

column4: ConcreteSpec/Spec/Prim.lean:288-295 (ObligationTable, ObligationTable.lookup) manually recurses over intrinsic obligation ids instead of List.find?, which ConcreteSpec/Spec/Basics.lean:7-13 mandates for named declaration tables. Codex confirmation of the aa44140a3 audit: s1c-4, table part of s2-1. Structural cause: declaration-table search bypasses the prescribed shared mechanism; no wrong-result example is established. Design: docs/proposals/ISS-0050-OBLIGATION-TABLE-SEARCH.md.
column7: ObligationTable.lookup delegates to List.find? on obligation.id = requested, or is deleted in favor of that search. Preserve first-match behavior and intrinsic-identity lookup laws; any retained independent view proves correspondence and has a premise-preserving search mutant distinguishing first from later duplicate matches.

column4: ConcreteSpec/Proofs/Own.lean:40-45 (Own.ResultSatisfies and decision instance), ConcreteSpec/Proofs/Grant.lean:17-25 (Generative.ResultSatisfies and instance), and :1009-1017 (Grants.ResultSatisfies and instance) independently define the same optional-result postcondition semantics. Own.StateResult, CallOwnResult and CallResult and their decision instances repeat it at ConcreteSpec/Proofs/Own.lean:20-37. Codex confirmation of the aa44140a3 audit: s6a-1, s6a-2. Structural cause: proof namespaces and specialized wrappers separately own the generic policy that none satisfies every postcondition and some applies it; the copies are definitionally equivalent today. Design: docs/proposals/ISS-0051-OPTIONAL-RESULT-POSTCONDITION.md.
column7: Give optional-result postcondition semantics and its decision procedure one reusable authoritative definition; generic and specialized wrappers delegate to it or are deleted. Any retained independent view proves correspondence for arbitrary result types and postconditions with a premise-preserving mutant that rejects none or ignores the successful value; preserve the specialized well-formedness postconditions.
